## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it is left running [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. That is a large load producing nothing, so standby is avoided unless boards are inside [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes]. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend, whereas a standby oven keeps burning 25.2 kW continuously [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

## Excess energy in incident S5

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. The weekend energy was about **1,556 kWh** versus about **346 kWh** normal, an excess of about **1,210 kWh** from a single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Note: the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit comes from switching the oven off proactively rather than waiting for an alarm [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

## Load Shedding Order (SOP-03)

**First load shed:** **EV charging (EV-01)** — pausing EV charging is Step 1 in the playbook order. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

The full shed order is:

| Order | Action | Equipment | Share of present load |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pause EV charging | EV-01 | 100% |
| 2 | Delay next burn-in loading | BI-01, BI-02 | 35% |
| 3 | Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C | CH-01, CH-02 | 4% |
| 4 | Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar | AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 | 3.5% |

[source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

**Loads that must NEVER be shed:**
- The **server room**
- **Running molders mid-cycle**
- **Reflow ovens with boards inside**

[source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-01_energy_policy.md#EM-01 Energy Policy > Operating principles]

Once demand is stable and back under the 1,125 kW warning line, these actions are restored in reverse order (pressure, setpoint, burn-in loading, then EV charging), not all at once. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 5: restore]
